title: Predictive usage/regression sentinel with causal correlator and incident orchestration
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Problem: We still see delayed detection of regressions in usage/cost/latency slices that only become actionable after customer impact. Current rule-based spike detectors generate noise for transient traffic changes and miss gradual regressions tied to config or model rollouts. Goal: build a predictive 'regression sentinel' that identifies likely ongoing regressions earlier, attributes probable causes, and triggers orchestrated alerts with adaptive suppression and automated remediation playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New sentinel produces alerts with >= 40% earlier detection time vs current guards on our historical Holdout set (Feb 2024-Feb 2026). 2) Precision >= 0.7 on synthetic-injection tests at operating thresholds. 3) Alerts include top-3 correlated factors (region, model_variant, autoscaler_event) and a recommended next step. 4) Console shows a per-alert diagnostic panel with time-series, decomposition, and causal factors. 5) End-to-end latency from detection to routed Slack + PagerDuty notification < 90s in staging.
design_summary: Pipeline overview: (A) Ingest per-minute rollup metrics (usage tokens, request count, p50/p95 latencies, cost accrual) into the sentinel pipeline from Kafka topics used by nightly aggregates. (B) Lightweight online decomposition per metric using STL-like seasonal + trend extraction tuned to customer cohort seasonality. (C) Probabilistic change-score via Bayesian change point detector (offline tuned) combined with exponential-weighted error residuals to detect persistent drift rather than transient spikes. (D) Causal correlator: when a regression signal is detected, run a fast conditional attribution using feature importance from a gradient-boosted model trained on historical incidents (features: model_version, region, instance_type, plan_tier, rollout_flag, recent-deploys, maintenance_windows). (E) Alert generation: assemble alert envelope with detection_score, confidence, top correlators, trend plots and suggested remediation (rollback, increase capacity, throttle back batching). (F) Orchestration: send to alert-routing service which applies policy (customer tier, ack window, escalation path) and kickstarts automated playbooks via the incident-runner service.
technical_notes:
- Windowing: use hierarchical windows (1m ingest -> 5m online aggregates -> 1h contextual aggregates) to keep compute low.
- Storage: keep 1m data for 14 days, 5m for 60 days, 1h for 540 days (aligns with cost reporting). Use existing TSDB with partition keys (customer, region, model_variant).
- Model training: nightly retrain of correlator on labeled incident table; seed features from console rollout metadata.
- Thresholding policy: detection_score > dynamic_threshold(percentile over last 28-day residual distribution) and persistence > 3 consecutive 5m buckets.
- Suppression: if same root cause exists for open incident from last 6h, suppress duplicates unless severity escalates.
- Rate/cost: estimated extra infra cost ~ $1.2k/mo for additional online workers at current scale; CPU-heavy attribution will be run on-demand with cached features to avoid steady load.
tradeoffs:
- Simpler rule-based detectors are cheaper but miss regressions tied to gradual config drift; ML correlator is more precise but requires labeled incidents and regular retraining.
- Attribution can produce false positives; to reduce noise we will expose correlator confidence and ask on-call to ratify before automated rollbacks.
- Keeping 1m resolution is costly; we compromise with 14-day high-res retention and aggressive downsampling.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement pipeline in staging with canary customer set (internal + 3 pilot customers) for 2 weeks. 2) Backfill two years of metrics into a parallel test instance and run synthetic-injection scenario tests. 3) Enable read-only console panels for SRE/PMs for 1 week. 4) Gradual alerting: first mode = 'detect-only' (no PagerDuty), second = 'ops-only' notifications, final = full routing with automated playbooks after 4-week stabilization. 5) Postmortem and metrics review after 6 weeks to tune thresholds.
testing_strategy:
- Backfill historical data and compute time-to-detect for all incidents in incident DB (2024-2026).
- Synthetic injection harness that simulates (a) sudden spikes, (b) slow-onset regressions, (c) multi-region rollouts.
- A/B evaluation vs existing detection pipeline instrumentation measuring precision/recall and mean time to detect.
- Chaos test: simulate delayed metric ingestion and verify graceful degradation (sentinel marks low-confidence and waits for reconciling windows).
runbook_snippet: If alert shows detection_score > 0.85 and correlator confidence > 0.6: 1) Acknowledge. 2) Check correlator top factors in diagnostic panel. 3) If 'recent-deploy' is top factor and multiple regions affected, open rollback PR and tag release on-call. 4) If 'autoscaler' or 'instance_type' present, run quick scale-up via infra console; if scale-up fails, trigger capacity-fallback policy. 5) Document action in incident ticket and mark as mitigated when 5 consecutive 5m buckets return to expected residual range.
metrics_to_track:
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for regressions.
- Precision & recall from synthetic injections.
- False positive rate per 10k customer-minutes.
- Average cost of sentinel per month.
- Number of automated playbook executions and success rate.
open_questions:
1) Should we onboard tenant-level models (per large-customer) or use a global correlator with tenant features? (biz/product vs infra cost tradeoff).
2) What's the acceptable ops noise budget? Propose allowing 1 FP per 30 days per on-call team.
3) Do we permit low-confidence automated rollbacks for P0 customer-impact incidents?
implementation_tasks: INGEST-PIPELINE: wire sentinel consumer to kafka.metrics.topic and implement 1m->5m aggregator lambda
DETECTOR-SERVICE: implement STL-like decomposition + bayesian change detector service (Go)
CORRELATOR: training job + inference endpoint (python/sql + xgboost)
ALERT-SHAPER: format alert envelope and small mutation to alert-router to accept correlator fields
CONSOLE: diagnostics panel and per-alert evidence visualizer
TEST-HARNESS: synthetic injection suite and historical backfill job
DOCS: design doc and runbook entry in Confluence
